title: Welcome Back: What Do You Remember?
goal: I can show what I remember about groups, facts and word problems.

card.desc: Bristol presents her Gratitude Project book. Then she does a review of Weeks 1–4: equal groups (multiply) or not (add), the fact tricks for 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 with missing factors, the 3 detective questions and price-tag problems. There is no new skill. Jonathan finds out what she kept over the break and what slipped.

win: Welcome back! Your brain kept so much!

slides.title: Welcome Back: On Your Own
slides.text: You showed your book. Now show what you remember, all on your own! 🧠

slides.title: Your tool box
slides.text: Use these on every question today.

steps.text: Equal groups → ✖️ multiply. Not equal → ➕ add.
Tricks: ×4 double, double. ×6 5s + one more group. ×7 5s + 2s. ×8 double the 4s. ×9 10s take away one group.
Detective: What is happening? Equal groups? Which operation?

slides.tip: Use your trick cards from class!

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say these out loud. You can tell your mom!
prompts: Tell your trick for the 8s and the 9s.
Tell a story where the groups are not equal.

items.q: Each plate has 6 cookies. How many cookies in all?
items.no: Count the plates. Each one has 6. Multiply.

items.q:
Are these groups equal?
Type equal or not equal.
items.why: The groups have 4, 6 and 3. They are not equal.
items.no: Count each group. Are they all the same?

items.q: These groups are not equal. Add them. How many stars in all?
items.no: Not equal means add. Add all three groups.

slides.title: Use your tricks
slides.text: Type the answer.

items.no: Use the 9s trick: 10 fours, take away one 4.
Use the 7s trick: the 5s fact plus the 2s fact.
Use the 8s trick: find 4 × 7, then double it.
What times 7 makes 49?
What times 8 makes 48?
What times 9 makes 36?

slides.title: Which operation?
slides.text: Read the whole story. Tap it. Then tap the right box.

items.text: There are 5 bikes. Each bike has 2 lights.
Liz baked 12 muffins. Her dad baked 8 more.
items.hint: Do the muffins join or go away?

items.text: Amy has 20 crayons. Marion has 13. How many more does Amy have?
Ellie had 16 balloons. 4 floated away.
items.hint: Did balloons join or go away?

items.text: Every one of the 6 frogs has 4 legs.
Marion read 9 pages before lunch and 6 pages after lunch.
items.why: 9 and 6 are different amounts that join. 9 + 6.

slides.title: Price tags
slides.text: Ask the 3 detective questions. Then type the number.

items.q: Hats cost $9 each. Ellie buys 4. What is the total?
items.no: Every hat is $9. Multiply. Then check your math.

items.q: Amy has $35. Kites cost $5 each. How many kites can she buy?
items.no: Count by 5s until you reach 35. Count the jumps.

items.q: A coat costs $41. A hat costs $16. How much more is the coat?
items.no: How much more means subtract. Then add back to check.
items.hint: Regroup a ten: 11 − 6 in the ones.

slides.title: Fix the mistake
slides.text: Type the right answer.

items.no: Use double, double. Then check your math.

sets.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
sets.why: The groups are 5, 3 and 6. Not equal, so add: 5 + 3 + 6 = 14.
no: Not every group has 6. Count each group.
The groups are not all 5. Count each group.

sets.no: Use the 8s trick: find 4 × 7, then double it.

sets.q:
Ellie found 8 shells. Then she found 7 more.
Add, subtract or multiply?
sets.why: 8 shells and 7 more shells join → add. 8 + 7 = 15.
sets.no: Do the shells join or go away? Are there equal groups?

sets.q: There are 7 tents. Each tent sleeps 4 kids. How many kids?
sets.no: Each tent has 4. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Marion had 42 beads. She used 17. How many are left?
sets.why: She used some, so subtract. 42 − 17 = 25. Check: 25 + 17 = 42.
sets.no: Beads went away. Subtract. Then add back to check.

sets.q: Liz has $25. Yo-yos cost $5 each. How many can she buy?
sets.no: Count by 5s until you reach 25. Count the jumps.

no: 48 is 6 × 8. Use the 6s trick: 5 × 7 = 35, plus one more 7.
49 is 7 × 7. Liz needs 6 sevens.

sets.why: The picture has 3 groups. Each group has 8. 3 × 8 = 24.
no: Count the groups in the picture. There are 3.
The picture shows equal groups, not 3 and 8 more.

sets.no: Use the 6s trick: the 5s fact plus one more 8.

sets.q:
There are 5 bunnies. Each bunny eats 3 carrots.
Add, subtract or multiply?
Ellie fills 9 vases. She puts 6 tulips in each vase. How many tulips?
sets.no: Each vase has 6. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Liz read 26 pages. Amy read 38 pages. How many more pages did Amy read?
sets.no: How many more means subtract. Then add back to check.

sets.q: Paint sets cost $9 each. Amy buys 3. What is the total?
sets.no: Every paint set is $9. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Marion buys 3 games at $8 each. Ellie buys 4 games at $6 each. Who spends more?
sets.why: Marion: 3 × 8 = 24. Ellie: 4 × 6 = 24. They spend the same.
no: Marion spends 3 × 8 = $24. Find Ellie's total: 4 × 6.
Ellie spends 4 × 6 = $24. Find Marion's total: 3 × 8.

sets.q: Look at the groups. Which is true?
sets.why: One group has only 3. Not equal, so add: 4 + 4 + 3 = 11.
no: Count the last group. It has 3, not 4.
Count the last group. It has 3, not 4.

sets.no: Use the 9s trick: 10 eights, take away one 8.

sets.q:
Marion had 24 grapes. She ate 9 of them.
Add, subtract or multiply?
sets.no: Did the grapes join or go away?

sets.q: There are 6 teams. Every team has 7 players. How many players?
sets.no: Every team has 7. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Amy has 19 red beads and 27 blue beads. How many beads in all?
sets.no: Add the red and the blue beads. Then check your math.

sets.q: Marion has $90. Lamps cost $10 each. How many lamps can she buy?
sets.no: Count by 10s until you reach 90. Count the jumps.

sets.q: Ellie says: 9 boxes. 7 cups in each box. 9 + 7 = 16 cups. What is right?
no: Ellie added. Each box has 7, so multiply.
56 is 8 × 7. There are 9 boxes.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Use your trick cards and the 3 detective questions.

questions.q: Each nest has 5 eggs. How many eggs in all?
questions.no: Count the nests. Each one has 5. Multiply.

questions.q: These groups are not equal. How many bugs in all?
questions.no: Not equal means add. Add all three groups.
Use the 6s trick: the 5s fact plus one more 4.
Use the 9s trick: 10 sevens, take away one 7.

questions.q: 7 × 4 has the same answer as which fact?
questions.why: Turn-around facts have the same answer. 7 × 4 = 4 × 7 = 28.
no: 7 × 5 = 35. That is one more group of 7.

questions.q: Liz has $50. Books cost $10 each. How many books can she buy?
questions.no: Count by 10s until you reach 50. Count the jumps.

questions.q: Ellie had 33 stickers. She gave 18 to Amy. How many does she have now?
questions.why: She gave some away, so subtract. 33 − 18 = 15. Check: 15 + 18 = 33.
questions.no: Stickers went away. Subtract. Then add back to check.
questions.hint: Regroup a ten: 13 − 8 in the ones.

questions.q: Which story is an equal groups story?
choices: There are 7 bowls with 5 berries in each.
no: Pens and pencils are different amounts. That is add.
She lost shells. That is subtract.
63 is 7 × 9. Marion needs 8 nines.
81 is 9 × 9. Marion needs 8 nines.

questions.q: Amy buys 2 hats at $9 each. Liz buys 4 hats at $4 each. Who spends more?
no: Liz spends 4 × 4 = $16. Find Amy's total: 2 × 9.
Find both totals. Are $18 and $16 the same?

questions.q: There are 6 cages. Each cage has 8 mice. Which number sentence fits?
no: Each cage has 8. That is equal groups, so multiply.
6 × 8 is not 42. 5 × 8 = 40. One more 8 is 48.

teacher.objective: Bristol presents her Gratitude Project book, then shows what she kept from Weeks 1–4 after the three-week break: equal groups → multiply and not equal → add; the fact tricks for 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 (mixed, with missing factors); the 3 detective questions; and price-tag problems (total, how many can I buy, who spends more). Week 5 (Review). No new skill. The goal is to find out what she kept and what slipped.
materials: The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)
Her Thankful Book and her Count the Slips page (page 3 of the Gratitude Project)
Play money: about 30 $1 bills and 8 $5 bills
5 index cards for her trick cards
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. Book and page 3 on the table.

plan.block: Show and Tell: My Thankful Book
plan.do: Class slide 2. She reads her book out loud and shows page 3. You are the audience. Praise one true thing.
Class slide 3. 6 piles of 5 → 6 × 5 = 30. River's pile of 4 → not equal → add (29).
Class slide 4. How the book ended, whether her guess from Lesson 11 was right, what Amy learned.
Class slide 5. She tells everything she remembers with no help. You check it off on the whiteboard.
Class slides 6–7. Beans in cups, then the sort. She says equal or not equal before each tap.
Class slides 8–9. She makes 5 trick cards, then solves 4 facts, saying the trick first.
Class slide 10. Skip count and count the jumps.
Class slides 11–12. The 3 questions, then she names the operation for 3 stories.
Class slides 13–15. Pay with play money, build 7 groups of $4, then 3 shop problems.
Class slide 16. She names each mistake before she picks.
Class slide 17. What was easy, what to practice. Show the task list.

watch: Facts that slipped over the break, most likely 7s and 8s (54 for 7 × 8, 48 for 6 × 7). Point to her trick card and have her say the trick before the answer.
Multiplying when the groups are not equal (6 × 5 for River's pile of 4). Have her count each group out loud.
Giving the last skip-count number instead of the number of jumps ("80" for how many puzzles). Ask: "Is 80 puzzles or dollars?"
Number grabbing in word problems: adding 4 + 7 when each bag has 7. Ask the 3 detective questions.
Regrouping slips in subtraction (42 − 17 as 35). Have her add back to check.
Mixing up the price (one) and the total (all).

packet_key.answer: Amy: 3 × 7 = 21. Liz: 4 × 5 = 20. Amy spends more ($1 more).
Any sentence about a page of her book, with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Write down what she could not say in the brain check (slide 5) and what she missed today. Those are the math items to keep alive in the recall slides of Lessons 13–18. If she scores under 85 on Show What You Know, have her redo the Practice set over the weekend and retake Show What You Know (she gets a new question set) before Lesson 13. If she did not pass the Pathways Week 7 Math retake from Lesson 11, do it with her today after class or at the start of Lesson 14 (in person). It is not on her task list because she does it with you.

tasks: Thursday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Friday: do the Lesson 12 Practice. Try to get 85 or more.
Saturday: do the Lesson 12 Packet, pages 1 and 2. Use your trick cards.
Sunday: do the reading lesson Pathways Week 1 Reading: Story Elements. Find the character and the setting in Theo's hiking story. Aim for 85. If it is locked, type 1111.
Friday, Saturday and Sunday: read your book for 15 minutes each day.

also.how: Reading practice for this week. Do it on Sunday (it is on your task list). Find the character and the setting in Theo's hiking story. Aim for 85 or more. If it is locked, type 1111.

slides.title: Welcome Back!
slides.text:
Welcome back from your break! 🎉
First, you show your Thankful Book.
Then we find out what you remember.

notes.do: Before she arrives, set out about 40 beans, 6 paper cups, play money ($1 and $5 bills), 5 index cards and the whiteboard. Ask her to put her Thankful Book and her Count the Slips page (page 3 of the project) on the table.
notes.say: "It has been three weeks! Today has two parts. First, your Thankful Book. Then a brain check. There is no new skill today. I want to see what you remember."
notes.ask: "Did you bring your book and your Count the Slips page?"
notes.listen: She has both. If page 3 is missing, ask her to tell you the numbers she remembers.

slides.title: My Thankful Book
slides.text: Read your book to your teacher. 📖
prompts: Read each page out loud. Show the picture.
Show your Count the Slips page. How many slips were in each pile?

notes.do: About 8 minutes. You are the audience. She reads the whole book out loud (about 3 minutes) and shows each picture. Then she shows page 3 (Count the Slips). Write her pile numbers on the whiteboard for the next slide.
notes.say: "Thank you for reading your book to me. You and your family worked hard on this."
notes.ask: "Which page is your favorite? Why?" "How many piles did you make? How many slips were in each pile?"
notes.listen: She reads each sentence smoothly and points to the picture. Praise one true thing: a capital letter, a period, a clear picture, a loud voice. Each person wrote one slip a day, so Week 1 piles should have about 5 slips each.

slides.title: Your slips are math!
slides.text: Each person wrote one slip a day for 5 days.

items.q: 6 piles. Each pile has 5 slips. Which number sentence finds all the slips?
no: That adds the 6 piles and the 5 slips. Every pile has 5, so multiply.
Count the piles. There are 6, not 5.

items.q:
One day, nobody wrote River's slip. Now his pile has only 4. Are the piles equal?
Type equal or not equal.
items.why: One pile has 4. The others have 5. They are not equal, so you add: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 4 = 29.
items.no: Count each pile. Do they all have the same number?

notes.do: If she has her real numbers from page 3, use them too. Equal piles: she multiplies. One pile different: she adds.
notes.ask: "Why can we multiply in the first picture?" "Why can't we multiply in the second picture?"
notes.listen: "Every pile has 5." "River's pile is different, so we add." If she says 6 × 5 for the second picture, have her count River's pile out loud.

slides.title: The end of the story
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: Did you finish the book? How did it end?
Last time you guessed the ending. Was your guess right?
What did Amy learn in this story?
starters: My guess was … It was right because …

notes.do: About 5 minutes. At Lesson 11 she guessed how the book would end. If she has not finished, she tells where she is and makes a new guess with a clue.
notes.ask: "How did it end?" "Was your guess right? What clue helped you?" "What did Amy learn?"
notes.listen: Events in order (first, next, then, at the end). For what Amy learned, accept a lesson in her own words. If she only retells, ask: "What would Amy do differently next time?"

slides.title: What do you remember?
slides.text: No looking back! Tell your teacher what you remember. 🧠
prompts: When do you multiply? When do you add?
Tell your trick for the 4s, 6s, 7s, 8s and 9s.

notes.do: About 4 minutes. Do not teach yet. On the whiteboard, make a quick list and check off what she says with no help: the equal groups rule, each of the 5 fact tricks, and the 3 questions. This is the main thing to find out today.
notes.say: "I want to see what stayed in your brain over the break. It is fine if something slipped. That tells me what to practice."
notes.listen: Equal groups → multiply, not equal → add. ×4: double, double. ×6: the 5s fact plus one more group. ×7: the 5s fact plus the 2s fact. ×8: double the 4s. ×9: the 10s fact take away one group. What is happening? Equal groups? Which operation? Circle anything she could not say. Spend the most time on those slides.

slides.title: Equal or not?
slides.text: Look at the groups first.

steps.text:
Equal groups: every group has the same number. → ✖️ multiply
4 vases. 3 roses in each. 4 × 3 = 12

Not equal: the groups are different. → ➕ add
3 roses, 5 roses, 2 roses. 3 + 5 + 2 = 10

slides.tip: Count every group before you choose.

notes.do: She builds both with beans in cups (4 cups of 3, then cups of 3, 5 and 2) before you reveal each step.
notes.listen: "No. The groups are not the same." If she says yes, line the three cups up and have her count each one.

slides.title: Multiply or add?
slides.text: Tap a card. Then tap the right box.

items.text: 5 plates. Each plate has 4 grapes.
One bag has 6 shells. One has 2. One has 7.
items.hint: Do all the bags have the same number?

items.text: 8 dogs. Every dog has 4 paws.
Liz has 9 beads. Amy has 5 beads.
items.hint: Do the girls have the same number?

items.text: 3 boxes with 7 crayons in each box.
A red cup has 4 beans. A blue cup has 8 beans.

notes.do: She reads each card out loud and says "equal" or "not equal" BEFORE she taps a box.
notes.ask: "Equal or not equal? How do you know?"
notes.listen: The words each and every point to equal groups. Two or three different numbers mean not equal, so add.

slides.title: Fact tricks
slides.text: You have a trick for every hard fact.

steps.text:
× 6: the 5s fact plus one more group.
6 × 9: 45 + 9 = 54

× 9: the 10s fact take away one group.
9 × 9: 90 − 9 = 81

slides.tip: Stuck on a fact? Use the trick. Do not count by 1s!

notes.do: Reveal one trick at a time. She writes each trick on an index card (5 cards). She keeps the cards for the packet.
notes.say: "These are your 5 tricks. Let's put each one on a card."
notes.ask: Before you reveal each one: "What is your trick for the 6s? the 7s?"
notes.listen: Check her list from the brain check. A trick she could not say before needs one more example out loud.

slides.title: Facts with tricks
slides.text: Say the trick out loud. Then type the answer.

items.no: Use the 6s trick: the 5s fact plus one more 6.
Use the 4s trick: double 7, then double again.
Use the 9s trick: 10 sevens, take away one 7.
Use the 8s trick: find 4 × 9, then double it.

notes.do: In person: she types on your laptop. She says the trick out loud before she types each answer.
notes.listen: 36, 28, 63, 72. On 7 × 9 she may use the 7s trick (35 + 28 = 63) or the 9s trick (70 − 7). Both are fine. If she counts by 1s, point to her index card.

slides.title: Find the missing factor
slides.text: What number makes the fact true?

items.no: What times 8 makes 64?
What times 9 makes 54?
What times 4 makes 28?
items.hint: Count by 4s until you reach 28. How many jumps?

notes.do: She skip counts on her fingers. For ____ × 4 = 28, she can put out 4 cups and add one bean to each cup at a time until there are 28 beans.
notes.listen: 8, 6, 7. The answer is the number of jumps, not the last number she says.

slides.title: The detective questions
slides.text: Before you solve a story, ask 3 questions. 🕵️

steps.text: 2. Are there equal groups? Look for each, every or per.
3. Which operation? ➕ add, ➖ subtract or ✖️ multiply?

Marion has 32 stickers. She gives 9 to Ellie.
Stickers go away → ➖ 32 − 9 = 23

slides.tip: How many more means compare. Compare means subtract.

notes.do: She says each question before you reveal it. On the last step, she answers all 3 questions out loud before you show the number sentence.
notes.ask: "What is happening to the stickers?" "How do we check 32 − 9 = 23?"

slides.title: Which operation?
slides.text: Type add, subtract or multiply.

items.q:
Ellie has 6 jars. She puts 5 shells in each jar. How many shells?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.why: 5 shells in each jar. Equal groups → multiply. 6 × 5 = 30.
items.no: Find the word each. Is every jar the same?

items.q:
Amy picked 14 apples. Liz picked 9 apples. How many more did Amy pick?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.no: This story compares two girls. What does how many more mean?

items.q:
The club washed 7 dogs on Saturday and 12 dogs on Sunday. How many dogs?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.why: 7 and 12 are different amounts that join → add. 7 + 12 = 19.
items.no: Are 7 and 12 equal groups? Do they join or go away?

notes.do: She reads each story out loud, answers the 3 questions, then types the operation.
notes.ask: Only if she is wrong: "What is happening? Are the groups equal?"
notes.listen: Multiply, subtract, add. The dogs story has two numbers but no equal groups, so it is add.

slides.title: Price tags
slides.text: Many things at the same price? Multiply. 🏷️

steps.text:
How many × price = total.
Pens cost $3 each. Amy buys 6. 6 × 3 = $18.

How many can I buy?
Ellie has $40. Bows cost $5 each. Count by 5s to 40. That is 8 jumps, so 8 bows.
Who spends more? Find both totals first. Then compare.

slides.tip: The price is for one. The total is for all of them.

notes.do: She pays for 6 pens at $3 with $1 bills in 6 piles of 3. Then she counts out $40 in $5 bills and counts the bills.
notes.ask: "Is $3 the price or the total?" "How many bills did you use for $40?"
notes.listen: $3 is the price, $18 is the total. 8 bills of $5 make $40, so 8 bows.

slides.title: Pay for the stickers
slides.text: Sticker sheets cost $4 each. Liz buys 7 sheets. Make one group of $4 for each sheet.
slides.hint: How many sheets? That is the number of groups. How much is each sheet?

notes.do: She makes 7 piles of four $1 bills on the table. Then she sets the counters on screen.
notes.ask: "How many groups? How many dollars in each? What is the total?"
notes.listen: 7 groups of 4, $28. If she makes 4 groups of 7, ask: "How many sheets did Liz buy?"

items.q: Notebooks cost $6 each. Marion buys 4. What is the total?
items.no: Every notebook is $6. Multiply. Then check your math.

items.q: Liz has $80. Puzzles cost $10 each. How many can she buy?
items.no: Count by 10s until you reach 80. Count the jumps.

items.q: Amy buys 5 pens at $3 each. Ellie buys 2 books at $7 each. Who spends more?
no: Ellie spends 2 × 7 = $14. Find Amy's total: 5 × 3.
Find both totals. Are $15 and $14 the same?

notes.do: She solves each one on the whiteboard first, then answers on the laptop.
notes.ask: "Too big or too small? How can you check?"
notes.listen: $24, 8 puzzles, Amy. On the last one she must find both totals before she picks.

no: 56 is 7 × 8. Use 10 × 6 = 60, then take away one 6.
63 is 9 × 7. Ellie needs 9 sixes, not 9 sevens.

items.q: Liz says: 4 bags. 7 apples in each bag. 4 + 7 = 11 apples. What is right?
no: Liz added. Each bag has 7, so multiply.
21 is 3 × 7. There are 4 bags.

notes.do: She says what Ellie and Liz did wrong BEFORE she picks.
notes.ask: "What did Ellie do? What did Liz do?"
notes.listen: Ellie used a wrong fact (56 is 7 × 8). Liz added when the groups were equal.

slides.title: What did you keep?
slides.text: You did a lot today! 🌟
prompts: What do you want to practice more?
Next lesson is about words like don't and can't. Can you find one in your book?

notes.do: Show the task list on the course page: tonight the After-Class Lesson; Friday the Practice; Saturday the Packet; Sunday the reading lesson; 15 minutes of reading each day.
notes.say: "You remembered a lot! Monday we start something new on Zoom."
notes.listen: She names one thing that was easy and one thing to practice. Compare it with your brain-check list.
